content:
I am happy to announce Nerodia, a Lean library for writing Python modules in pure Lean, and its companion project, setuptools-lean, a setuptools plugin for packaging them. They are inspired by Rust's PyO3 and maintained by the Lean FRO. Nerodia is released as a preview with a limited API, but a complete packaging workflow. We are looking for early adopters to provide feedback on the design and build process. Please file any issues you encounter on the relevant repository.

Nerodia allows those most familiar with Lean to create and distribute Lean-based Python modules with little to no experience extending Python. Users define the Python interface in Lean and then ship it as a Python package. A worked example can be found in Nerodia's README.

To provide a taste, a Python module can be defined like so:

module
import Nerodia
open scoped Nerodia

py_module "string_sum"

/-- Formats the sum of two numbers as a string. -/
@[py_module_fn "sum_as_string"]
def sumAsString (a b : Nat) : String :=
  toString (a + b)

And then, with a single declarative pyproject.toml, it can be run immediately:

$ uv run python
>>> import string_sum
>>> string_sum.sum_as_string(5, 20)
'25'
>>> string_sum.sum_as_string.__doc__
'Formats the sum of two numbers as a string.'

It is recommended to use uv to run Python, as it is a modern Python package manager that makes the process even more seamless. Nonetheless, Nerodia should equally support other setups.

Nerodia also automatically generates Python type stubs. Thus, editing a Python module that imports a Nerodia module will provide all the rich type information and docstrings users might expect from regular Python code.

(Logo created by @Sofia Rodrigues)
